candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is serum sickness as a whole entity. Hemolytic anemia due to streptokinase is a narrower, single-manifestation label that misses the systemic immune-complex syndrome (fever, arthralgia, elevated ESR/CRP) defining serum sickness.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Hemolytic anemia is a possible component/manifestation of serum sickness but does not capture the full syndrome; also the anemia here may be multifactorial

candidate_relations.reason: The patient received streptokinase two weeks prior and now presents with fever, arthralgia, elevated inflammatory markers, and sterile cultures — classic serum sickness. Adding the etiology (streptokinase) is a harmless, clinically accurate specification that does not conflict with the reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Specifies both the syndrome (serum sickness) and the causative agent (streptokinase), fully consistent with the reference

candidate_relations.reason: Same reasoning as C001; focuses on a single hematologic finding rather than the systemic immune-complex disease. The Hb of 9.65 g/dL could reflect hemolysis but the overall picture points to serum sickness.

candidate_relations.reason: Reactive thrombocytosis can occur in serum sickness or inflammatory states, but drug-induced thrombocytosis as a standalone diagnosis does not capture the systemic immune-complex syndrome that is the reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Extreme thrombocytosis (platelets 4,456,000/µL) is a laboratory finding present in this case but is a manifestation/association rather than the primary diagnosis

candidate_relations.reason: While the patient has rheumatic heart disease history and joint pain, anti-CCP is negative, there is no evidence of recent streptococcal infection, no Jones criteria fulfilled (no carditis flare, no chorea, no subcutaneous nodules, no erythema marginatum), and the temporal link to streptokinase administration strongly favors serum sickness over rheumatic fever.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Rheumatic fever is a distinct post-streptococcal immune-mediated disease with different diagnostic criteria
